_about: The specialties of the league. Since the options overhaul (Sept 26, 2026) there is ONE: the options desk (alpaca-options), on the Brokerage Account and its practice account; every Kalshi, crypto, equity and open desk left with the prune (the pre-overhaul list is kept for the old tests as league/tests/fixtures/niches_legacy.json until Wave 2b rewrites them). An agent belongs to its specialty for life and its children inherit it: the House shows it only this universe, refuses entries outside it and tags its research with it. The swarm (Wave 4) replaces desks with families. Previous text: The specialties of the league. An agent belongs to one for life and its children inherit it: the House shows it only this universe, refuses entries outside it, tags its research with it and pays niche floors by it. A Kalshi universe is the series listed here (real tickers, ranked by the 24-hour volume of their markets that resolve within 48 hours; surveyed Sept 19, 2026: 736 series, $63M a day) plus any series the House's daily survey finds that matches `patterns` (and `category`, which Kalshi reports per series), so a universe follows the sporting calendar without an edit. Each specialty is one partner's DESK, named for a figure of the firm the league is named after; every agent of a desk is numbered from that name (meriwether, meriwether-2 ...) and a child takes the next free number in the line, as the first run's desks were Mullins VI and VIII. Sept 23, 2026: seats follow evidence -- the weather desk (the one mechanism earning real money) takes 10 and prices 8, the 24/7 crypto desks 8 (Kalshi) and 12 (Alpaca), and the hourly ETF and megacap desks 12, beside a population of 96; three replay-passing foundry cards had waited for seats on full desks. Sept 23, 2026 (the open desks): `kalshi-open` and `alpaca-open` (`open: true`) hold every tradable market of their venue -- any Kalshi series but the multivariate combos (`exclude_patterns`), any US stock, ETF or coin against the dollar (`asset_classes`; never options) -- list nothing, plant no founders and take 8 seats each. A program is born there only when no one desk holds most of what its NEEDS name (`niches.match`, `niches.spanning`); what it is shown when it names nothing it may trade is a capped discovery list (Kalshi: the daily survey's busiest series, those no desk claims first; Alpaca: the other Alpaca desks' symbols, coins first). Sept 23, 2026 (the learn-and-unblock run, the seat market follows evidence): 16 seats were free on desks nobody graduates into (strikes 2 of 8, megacaps 8 of 12, the open desks 0 of 8) while the desks with waiting lab graduates were full, and `kalshi-weather` was the only desk with a positive forward record (7 of 10 living W_paper > 1; the two real earners). So weather 10 -> 14, sports 12 -> 16, index ETFs 12 -> 14, 15-minute crypto 8 -> 10; the graveyards shrink: crypto strikes 8 -> 4 (40 born, 2 passed replay, -10.3% a block), sports props 6 -> 4 (34 born, 5 passed) and attention 4 (34 born, 2 passed; it had no cap and took the default 5). The sum of the caps (134) stays above the population (112). Sept 24, 2026 (the close-the-gaps run, R2: capacity follows the waiters that remain once the search has closed its desks). Measured at 15:06Z: 82 newcomers waited in a league of 112 of 112, every desk they waited for full; 21 leave the queue (the 20 of kalshi-crypto-15m, which the search closes, and a graduate whose forward window loses) and Deploy C's lab holds 17 nudges, so 44 remain. Seats follow them: megacaps 12 -> 16 (4 graduates, the longest 24.5 h, one with a winning forward window), index ETFs 14 -> 18 (9: 2 graduates, 3 cards, a retained candidate, 3 corrected children), weather 14 -> 17 (the longest card, 47.3 h, and the retained candidates of mullins-14, +38.4% on 113 replay trades, and mullins-25), crypto alts 12 -> 16 (4 cards and 4 corrected children; its 12 seats are 9 winners and 3 real-money probes: only a new seat seats them), sports props 4 -> 6 (the retained candidates of hufschmid-28 and -30, +44% and +91% on 29 and 33 replay trades), crypto strikes 4 -> 6 (the search reopened it on two lab families positive there, 17 and 7 active blocks, one on real money; 17 wait for it and 3 of its 4 seats are real money: two seats, not the old 8, since its pre-lab record was the floor's worst), and sports 16 -> 19 for the proven family's births (R3: its program runs on one member of four). Fewer where the search is closed: 15-minute crypto 10 -> 8 (every family negative there; the five 15-minute probes lost $27.29 on 23 settlements that day), and the House holds a closed desk's cap at its members until a family there turns positive (`House._follow_the_search`). The sum of the caps (154) stays above the population's ceiling (128, while Sail's runway holds).

niches.title: Listed options on Alpaca: long calls and puts, and structures with defined risk on practice
niches.brief: Calls and puts on sixteen liquid underlyings and, ON PRACTICE since Sept 25, 2026, level-3 STRUCTURES WITH DEFINED RISK. SINGLE CONTRACTS are LONG PREMIUM ONLY: you open by buying and close by selling, so the most a position can lose is what was paid. One contract is 100 shares and cannot be cut smaller; an order is capped at $75 on practice and $20 with real money, so the single premiums in reach are under 75 cents (20 cents with real money): at-the-money weeklies on stocks under about $20 (F, SOFI, AAL, RIVN, SNAP, VALE) and out-of-the-money contracts on the rest. No single-contract entry expires today; the House sells a single contract still held at 14:30 New York on its last day. STRUCTURES: a strategy whose NEEDS carry "structures": true is a STRUCTURE AGENT; its book holds structures only (a single-leg intent from it is refused). Admitted: debit and credit verticals, iron condors and iron butterflies, long butterflies, calendars and diagonals, long straddles and long strangles, on one underlying, 2-4 legs, whole contracts. Refused always: a naked short leg, any ratio but a butterfly's body of 2, a broken wing, a diagonal whose long leg is less favourable, legging in or out. An intent names `structure`, `action` (open or close; a close names the same legs and closes the whole structure), `legs` ({occ, role: long|short}), `quantity` and `limit_price`: the NET a share as a trader says it (opening, the most debit to pay or the LEAST credit to take; closing, the least to receive or the most to pay to buy it back); league/CONTRACT.md, Options structures. HOW IT IS HELD: as ONE position priced at S = its net value + K, K zero for a debit structure and the widest wing for a credit one, so what opening costs is the structure's maximum loss: a $1-wide SPY iron condor sold for 0.38 is held at 0.62, $62 at risk. The caps ($75 an order and $100 a position on practice) meter exactly that, a structure is marked at its bid, and a sale that leaves it flat is ONE closed trade. The book refuses a limit more than 10% from the structure's touch: when your exit fires, close near the bid rather than resting a far target. The fee assumed: $0.05 a contract a leg a fill (a vertical $0.10, a condor $0.20). TIME: a structure's clock is its EARLIEST expiry; no structure is opened on that day from 14:30 New York, the House sells whatever is still held from 15:30 New York that day at its bid, re-priced each tick, and nothing is held into an expiry. Write your own profit target, stop and time exit: only a close makes realized P&L, and 0-7 day expiries on SPY, QQQ and IWM ($1 strikes) are the point. WHAT THE HOUSE SHOWS: a single-contract agent `ctx["chain"]`, contracts on its underlyings expiring after today, within a fifth of the stock's price, two-sided and affordable in one order; a structure agent `ctx["chain"]` from TODAY (0 DTE until 14:30 New York) to `max_days_to_expiry`, within a fifth of the price, at most 80 contracts an underlying nearest the money, NOT limited to what one contract may cost, and `ctx["structures"]`: ready-made adjacent-strike debit and credit verticals and iron condors that fit its caps, with their net bid and ask, opening limit, maximum loss and gain, days to expiry and deltas; a held structure shows its type, legs, natural open price, mark and P&L. Rows carry bid, ask, implied volatility and delta where the feed has them; daily bars and the touch of each underlying. The House is configured for SIP stock bars/quotes and OPRA option chains/quotes (check runtime_status for the deployed feed); a rejected data request is unavailable data, never silently indicative quotes. A limit order bounds its price but does not establish depth or remove adverse selection. EVERYTHING ON STRUCTURES IS PRACTICE until the owner's switch (O1): a structure on real money is refused. REPLAY: Alpaca holds option trade bars since Jan 18, 2024 and NO historical option quotes; where the House's options history covers your underlyings a candidate is replayed on quotes ESTIMATED from prints and conservative fills (long legs at the ask or worse, short legs at the bid or worse, the fee on every leg; CONTRACT.md), and elsewhere practice is this specialty's replay. What is known: nothing by this firm. Published: option BUYERS lose on average, because they pay the spread and the variance premium (implied volatility runs above realised); defined-risk SELLERS collect that premium and carry the tail, capped at the wing. A specialist should learn which underlyings keep structure spreads tight, how much of a credit time decay pays per hour at 0-2 days, how implied compares with realised volatility before and after earnings, and when a trend makes a debit vertical cheaper than the move.
